description:
Why do so many animals at the bottom of the sea grow so big? Doug rides a winch cable from 250 meters down to the deepest trench on Earth and meets the deep sea giants on the way: the giant oarfish, the colossal squid, a Greenland shark that may be nearly 400 years old, the giant isopod that went five years without eating, and, at 10,641 meters, a giant cell. Along the way: what scientists think actually causes deep-sea gigantism, and why they still argue about it.

Where in the ocean should Doug sink next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you're here for Doug's next bad idea.
